intro: Bosnia and Herzegovina is home to three main peoples, Bosniaks, Serbs and Croats, who speak very similar languages but mostly follow different faiths.

chapters.title: Three peoples
text: Bosniaks, mostly Muslim, are the largest group, followed by Serbs, mostly Orthodox Christian, and Croats, mostly Catholic. Their languages, Bosnian, Serbian and Croatian, are almost the same.
In Sarajevo, a mosque, an Orthodox church, a Catholic cathedral and a synagogue stand within a few minutes' walk of each other, and the city has been called 'the Jerusalem of Europe'.

chapters.title: Daily life
text: Many young people have moved abroad for work. Coffee, served in small copper pots, is a social ritual.

keyTerms.meaning: A member of the mostly Muslim South Slavic people of Bosnia.
